FT Nvidia falls after SEC probe on potential accounting issues European stocks end a bruising week. German DAX falls 7.29%. Trump: Secured two new trade deals. 10 others coming very soon. Core up 1.0% vs 0.7% estimate. Morning Kickstart. Anthropic slides after its IPO and gold breaks lower investingLive European news wrap: Stock markets remain under pressure, bonds rally on slowdown expectations North American market wrap | Friday, November 20, 2026 Stocks got hammered into the close. Anthropic gave back much of its first-day gain, and Nvidia’s losses deepened after Reuters reported that the SEC was examining the chipmaker’s accounting practices. The selling spread across the AI trade, from semiconductors to data-center suppliers. The Nasdaq Composite lost 1,261 points and wiped out its gains for the year. The S&P 500 fell for a seventh straight session. Treasuries and the yen caught a bid, but lower yields did little to slow the selling in stocks. Gold, silver and Bitcoin fell alongside equities. Oil went the other way as renewed U.S.–Iran escalation risk kept traders focused on supply through the Strait of Hormuz. FX. Yen leads, Aussie lags The dollar was mixed, with the dollar index nearly flat at 103.891 late in the session. The USD was weakest against the yen, with USDJPY down 0.71% to 158.54, and strongest against the Australian dollar, with AUDUSD down 0.57% to 0.6618. USDCHF fell 0.43% to 0.8402. The USD gained against the kiwi and edged higher against the Canadian dollar. EURUSD and GBPUSD were both flat. USDJPY covered 142 pips, 156% of its 22-day average daily range. AUDUSD reached 140% of its average and USDCHF reached 116%. EURUSD and GBPUSD covered just 66% and 75% of their averages, respectively. Treasuries. The 10-year is back below 5% 2-year 4.649%, −13.0 basis points 5-year 4.7403%, −12.6 basis points 10-year 4.9438%, −10.8 basis points 30-year 5.3298%, −7.1 basis points The front end led the move lower in yields, steepening the curve. The 2-year fell 13 basis points even after Fed Governor Lisa Cook argued for tighter policy. The bid for Treasuries held as stocks made new lows. images.investinglive.com. Will the Fed save the market or will they fight inflation? Pres Trump wants the Fed to ease policy despite the inflation? The chance of a Fed stands pat in December is close to 9% now. U.S. stocks. A bruising end to the week Dow industrial average 48,147.33, −1.93% Friday, −8.0% for the week. S&P 500 6,910.39, −3.70% Friday, −8.6% for the week. Nasdaq Composite 22,617.73, −5.28% Friday, −10.0% for the week. Russell 2000 2,581.79, −2.76% Friday, −7.5% for the week. Nasdaq 100 −5.6% Friday, −10.4% for the week. AI and chips take the biggest hit Nvidia closed down 13.8%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.7%. The selling reached beyond chips. AI cloud provider CoreWeave fell 12.1%, and Bloom Energy dropped 15.3%. Anthropic fell 9.1% to $88.30 in its second session, still above its $83 IPO price. General Mills gained 3.7% as consumer staples found some buyers. investinglive.com Europe. DAX leads the declines German DAX 24,801.22, −2.60% Friday, −7.29% for the week. French CAC 40 7,927.75, −1.89% Friday, −5.27% for the week. UK FTSE 100 10,346.33, −1.02% Friday, −5.10% for the week. Spanish IBEX 35 18,873.09, −1.63% Friday, −5.73% for the week. Italian FTSE MIB 48,703.73, −2.48% Friday, −6.08% for the week. investinglive.com U.S. data and the Fed Final November University of Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 from 48.0 in October. The bigger move was in one-year inflation expectations, which fell to 3.7% from 4.3% in the preliminary report and 4.7% in October. Five-year expectations eased to 3.3% from 3.5% in October. Cook said September’s rate hike had done too little to curb inflation and warned that waiting could make it harder to bring inflation down. investinglive.com Oil rises as Iran risk returns to focus WTI was up 1.53% at $83.70 late in the session, and Brent was up 0.71% at $92.63. The Financial Times reported that President Trump was weighing renewed strikes on Iran. The risk of disruptions through Hormuz helped support crude even as the equity selloff raised questions about demand. investinglive.com Gold, silver and copper slide Gold fell 2.41% to $3,537.77, silver dropped 3.84% to $41.224 (remember when it surged to $121 at the beginning of the year?), and copper lost 3.01% to $5.4640 and trades lower on the year now. A flat dollar index and falling Treasury yields would ordinarily help gold. Its decline alongside equities is consistent with investors raising cash. The heavier losses in silver and copper also fit with concerns about industrial demand. investinglive.com Bitcoin breaks $60,000 Risk off. Bitcoin was down 4.86% at $58,902 late in the session. It traded with the broader selloff in risk assets, and the break below $60,000 added pressure to Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood. What I’m watching Monday Can chip stocks hold a bounce with the Nasdaq indices closing just above the 100 week MAs, and does the 10-year yield stay below 5%? Those are two quick reads on whether Friday’s selling is easing. Oil remains the market to watch for any weekend developments around Hormuz. The next U.S. growth check comes with Monday’s flash PMIs at 9:45 a.m. ET. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

articles.title: ‘Inside Deutsche Bank’ Exposes Questionable Practices
articles.content: ‘Inside Deutsche Bank’ Exposes Questionable Practices | theTrumpet.com ‘Inside Deutsche Bank’ Exposes Questionable Practices ‘Inside Deutsche Bank’ Exposes Questionable Practices Barcex via Wikimedia Commons, Emma McKoy/Trumpet ‘Inside Deutsche Bank’ Exposes Questionable Practices nside Deutsche Bank,” an investigation conducted by 200 journalists across dozens of media platforms and published beginning Tuesday, has exposed questionable business practices by Germany’s largest bank. The investigation is based on 15 million internal documents leaked by two anonymous whistleblowers who believed Deutsche Bank was committing crimes. are focusing on the bank’s ties with Jeffrey Epstein and Russian oligarchs; however, the leaks also reveal a trail of potentially unethical practices in other areas. Deutsche Bank failed to properly vet high-risk Colombian transactions. An internal probe found it filed fewer than 10 suspicious activity reports on 171,000 transactions worth about €20 billion to nine Colombian banks in 2019, and a later sample of 4,800 of those transactions identified 230 that should have been flagged. , who oversaw Deutsche Bank’s debt operations in Argentina and South America, became Argentina’s financing undersecretary in 2016. The documents show the bank’s Anti-Financial Crime unit warned of conflicts of interest. Yet Deutsche Bank still won large underwriting and loan contracts while Bausili served in the Ministry of Treasury and Public Finance, and it paid him $180,000 in deferred compensation. (He later became governor of Argentina’s central bank.) The documents also reveal that Deutsche Bank had loose due diligence measures for royals from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates and set up offshore accounts to protect them from regulators. It also potentially engaged in bribery, according to news platform Daraj, as well as conflicts of interest and nepotism by employing relatives of Gulf state royalty. German businesses are typically held in high regard despite Deutsche Bank’s poor reputation among regulators. People have largely forgotten its bending of the rules, its numerous scandals relating to market manipulation and money laundering, and the $20 billion in fines and settlements against it over the past 26 years. The revelations from this investigation further expose this esteem to be wrong. Copyright © 2026 Philadelphia Church of God, All Rights Reserved

articles.title: Decade of Peace, Compassion & Imagination: The Founding of Live Good & the 10-Year Anniversary of The Noah’s Ark Blanket
articles.desc: Live Good CEO Jennifer Chi reflects on the founding of her company and why the message behind the Noah’s Ark baby blanket resonates with so many today.
articles.content: Decade of Peace, Compassion & Imagination: The Founding of Live Good & the 10-Year Anniversary of The Noah’s Ark Blanket There were 1,629 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 504,826 in the last 365 days. Decade of Peace, Compassion & Imagination: The Founding of Live Good & the 10-Year Anniversary of The Noah’s Ark Blanket Live Good Noah's Ark: "Together We Thrive" Celebrating 10 Years of Noah's Ark Blanket The Live Good Peace Dove: A New Beginning Live Good CEO Jennifer Chi reflects on the founding of her company and why the message behind the Noah’s Ark baby blanket resonates with so many today. IRVINE, CA, UNITED STATES, November 20, 2026 / / -- Ten years ago, in a quiet warehouse with bright white walls and a single desk, Live Good CEO Jennifer Chi envisioned a world where animals of every kind gathered together in peace. “The idea came from seeing the world through the eyes of a child, where diverse animals come together in harmony to weather a storm,” Jennifer explains on the 10-year anniversary of the Noah’s Ark baby blanket. During those early years, the company founder would spend hours sketching a playful animal kingdom for the Endangered Species baby line and pairing the soft, earthy color palettes that would define the next bedding collection. She did her most creative thinking while sitting alone in an empty warehouse. “I always felt like I was inside a white canvas where my imagination was safe and free to explore new ideas,” she recalls of the original Live Good warehouse. One afternoon, as she wondered how to unite the creatures from her Endangered Species collection, a new image began to take shape: a gathering of animals aboard a single vessel. Only later did she recognize the familiar childhood story emerging from her imagination was that of Noah’s Ark. “Until that moment, I had not thought of the Noah's Ark legend in more than 20 years. I used to love that story when I was a little girl because it seemed to hold a certain truth: We are all in this together. No one life is more important than another. Every living thing is sacred and should be protected.” Although the story of Noah’s Ark carries different cultural and religious interpretations, Live Good founder’s inspiration centered on its universal themes of compassion, coexistence, and responsibility for the natural world. The Peace Dove: Where the Live Good Story Began Long before creating the Noah’s Ark baby blanket, Jennifer’s creative journey began with a single image, a dove carrying a leaf in its mouth. During a deeply personal period of reflection, following years of witnessing difficult aspects of humanity through her previous work as a human rights investigator, Jennifer envisioned a new beginning rooted in goodness, innocence, and peace. The words “Live” and “Good” echoed in her mind, along with the vivid image of a dove. “In those early days, I had no idea what the message behind these recurring images truly meant. After years of witnessing the worst of humanity in my previous work, and even in my own life, I felt a deep need to start over. Live Good was born from a desire to wipe the slate clean… to wash the world away… It was about finding a way to begin again with only the purest living things inhabiting a new world.” The vivid image became the Live Good Peace Dove, the very first animal Jennifer created which is the original logo for the company. Today, the dove remains part of Live Good's identity, appearing on the fabric tag sewn into every product. The animals featured on the Noah’s Ark baby blanket also hold special meaning. Each comes from Live Good's Endangered Species baby pillow collection, bringing together beloved characters in a shared celebration of wildlife and the importance of protecting the natural world. A decade after the blanket's creation, its inspiration remains as meaningful as ever. For the Live Good community, the Noah’s Ark baby blanket is an expression of hope and renewal. articles.title: JPMorgan Chase to Support Customers Affected by Cyber Attack
articles.desc: JPMorgan Chase will contact customers affected by a cyberattack to provide assistance to help minimize exposure to personal data
articles.content: JPMorgan Chase to Support Customers Affected by Cyber Attack - News247Plus JPMorgan Chase will contact customers affected by a cyberattack to provide assistance to help minimize exposure to personal data The security of personal data is again under pressure in the financial sector. A new technological breach has alerted some of the country’s leading banks and payment networks, in an episode that has raised concerns about the exposure of private information and possible fraud attempts against their customers. JPMorgan Chase, considered the largest bank in the , confirmed that some of its customer data was exposed after hackers hacked the systems of external supplier companies. In the face of this situation, the institution announced that it will contact the injured persons directly and offer them assistance, including a free credit monitoring service. The entity explained that support will be available “when appropriate”, in reference to users whose personal information has been compromised. Preliminary investigations indicate that the attackers managed to access marketing and contact records that were stored on the platforms of their contractors. Potentially exposed information includes names and email addresses. However, a Reuters review of the files disclosed by the cyberbullying group identified more than 16,000 customer emails, some accompanied by phone numbers and postal codes, as well as 124 corporate addresses that apparently belong to bank employees. Newsweek magazine noted that the records could be related to JPMorgan Chase’s Reserve program, a credit card available on invitation and generally aimed at people with at least $10 million in assets under management. Although the compromised information would not include bank card data, email addresses can become a tool for preparing phishing attacks and other attempts to supplant identity. Criminals could take advantage of that data to send fraudulent messages that appear to come from JPMorgan Chase or other financial institutions. Therefore, the bank asked to be suspicious of suspicious communications and to avoid opening links whose origin cannot be verified. The institution also assured that its central operations did not suffer damage and that its services continue to operate normally. So far, it has not publicly identified the contractors affected, nor has it specified when the intrusion occurred. The problem is not limited to JPMorgan Chase. Visa and Mastercard also information exposures linked to external providers, although both companies ruled out affecting their payment processing networks. Visa linked the incident to a service provider in the Asia-Pacific region, while Mastercard confirmed that a limited amount of emails and other non-payment data was exposed among a small group of participants in a benefit program. In all three cases, the companies argued that card numbers and payment infrastructure were not compromised. JPMorgan Chase also clarified that this breach has "no connection" to the interruptions experienced by some customers when carrying out banking operations at the beginning of the week. According to the institution, those problems were solely due to a “software failure.” The coincidence occurs in a difficult week for U.S. technology services. Recent incidents include Microsoft email interruptions, flight suspension ordered by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and problems in National Security Agency (NSA) classified internal banking systems and communications. Following the financial interruptions, the Office of the Currency Controller (OCC) consulted different entities to know the scope of the failures and the communication with their clients. Meanwhile, administration officials noted that there is no evidence linking recorded technology cuts to cyber attacks. articles.title: Caribbean Corals Are in Crisis. Fossil Reefs Can Help Point to Where Corals May Persist
articles.desc: The post Caribbean Corals Are in Crisis. Fossil Reefs Can Help Point to Where Corals May Persist appeared first on UT News.
articles.content: Caribbean Corals Are in Crisis. Fossil Reefs Can Help Point to Where Corals May Persist - UT News Caribbean Corals Are in Crisis. Fossil Reefs Can Help Point to Where Corals May Persist Lead author of the study Claire Williams installs a light and temperature logger at a coral reef site in Portland, Jamaica. Photo by Rowan Martindale. The fossilized remains of ancient coral reefs often sit just meters from living corals in the Caribbean, where reefs have declined sharply over the past 70 years. Those fossils could help show where corals might survive a warming future. In two new papers, researchers at The University of Texas at Austin identify which coral species dominated ancient reefs in northeastern Jamaica and suggest how that record could guide reef rehabilitation. “Because we were studying already damaged reefs (in the modern-day Caribbean), we had a limited baseline of what a healthy reef used to look like and were missing understandings of things like resilience,” said Claire Williams, who led research on the fossil and modern reefs while earning a doctorate at the UT Jackson School of Geosciences. “So, my theory was that by bringing in the fossil record, we could get a richer picture of coral tolerances and make better predictions for the future.” . At two sites in Jamaica, the team analyzed the corals found in fossil reefs dating back to 125,000 to 130,000 years ago — the Late Pleistocene epoch — a time known for interglacial warming periods. According to Williams, these past warming periods are good analogs for what the planet is projected to experience in about 50 to 100 years. The fossil reefs are now above sea level, so the researchers adapted a transect method used to monitor modern corals: Instead of swimming above the reefs, the researchers walked along them, photographing the fossils to estimate the number and distribution of corals in an area. They then compared this data from fossil reefs with coral species at modern sites. At the modern sites, the researchers found that certain branching corals called Acropora — including — which were abundant during the Pleistocene, are now largely dead and covered by algae. What’s more, most remaining corals are , a globular species that Williams said can recover quickly after disturbances but doesn’t provide helpful reef structure. “These big branching species provide a lot of habitat and offshore protection. With that gone, we’ve lost that function on the reef,” Williams said. The solution to rebuilding the reef isn’t as simple as planting more corals in degraded reef environments, said co-author Rowan Martindale, an associate professor at the Jackson School’s Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences “We can nurture and transplant new, healthy corals from nurseries to damaged reefs, often referred to as coral gardening, but if they are in a place that’s too hot in the future, they’re not going to survive,” Martindale said. “Many of the Alligator Head Foundation’s transplanted corals died off during the heat-induced bleaching event in the summer of 2023.” (The Alligator Head Foundation is a marine conservation group in East Portland, Jamaica.) With that in mind, the researchers also conducted a study on the ecological niches of ancient corals, analyzing the water temperature and salinity the corals could tolerate. In this analysis, they included data from mid-Holocene fossil records to get data points from a more recent period, 5,000 to 7,000 years ago. This data was then used to predict the places with similar ecological niches to these past environments — helping to indicate where the species might survive in the future. The researchers also incorporated data from climate models to identify reef areas in the Caribbean that are projected to have the salinity and sea-surface temperature best suited for species that can help foster and grow healthy reef ecosystems in the future. articles.title: Claude helped crack the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, Anthropic researcher claims
articles.desc: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude helped prove the 167-year-old Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
articles.content: Claude helped prove 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, researcher claims Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims Claude helped prove the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, extending the original 1859 conjecture. The proposed proof comes with an extensive Lean archive containing approximately 175,187 source files and 239MB of data. Lean checks mathematical arguments against formal logical rules, but independent researchers must still verify the complete proof. An Anthropic mathematician claims he has solved one of mathematics’ most difficult problems with help from Claude. Levent Alpöge announced the proposed proof on Friday, November 20, potentially bringing a 167-year mathematical mystery closer to resolution. The claim concerns the Riemann hypothesis, a foundational conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers. Alpöge says his work goes further, establishing the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). However, independent mathematicians must still examine the proof before anyone can declare the problem solved. Alpöge published a four-page explanation alongside an extensive collection of Lean verification files. The archive reportedly contains approximately 239 megabytes of data and 175,187 source files. Lean is a formal proof assistant that checks mathematical arguments against established logical rules. Its verification system allows researchers to examine whether each step follows from the preceding assumptions. In his explanation, Alpöge credited Claude with making rapid progress during the final stages. He described an approach involving weighted prime sums, known as von Mangoldt sums. The proposed method also uses mathematical constructions called theta lifts. The mathematician acknowledged the emotional significance of potentially resolving such an influential problem. He described the development as losing a guiding light for mathematical research. However, he also expressed excitement about the scientific possibilities ahead. New OpenAI benchmark tests how well models reason through complex drug discovery tasks Trump warns US tech firms of massive taxes for overseas data centers amid China fears New underwater robot dives 328 feet deep to spot hull damage before it sinks your trip The Next Phase of Robotics: From Technological Progress to Real-World Impact US firm unveils Phantom MKII battlefield humanoid robot with bigger payload, tougher build A Lean archive offers stronger evidence than an ordinary AI-generated mathematical explanation. However, compiling the code does not automatically establish that the intended conjecture has been proven. An independent verification project has reportedly confirmed that the downloaded files match Alpöge’s published archive. Its initial checks also found that the main theorem statements compile against Mathlib, Lean’s standard mathematics library. However, researchers must still examine the complete proof. They need to establish that the code addresses the conventional Riemann hypothesis. They must also check its mathematical definitions and identify any unsupported assumptions. The distinction matters because Alpöge claims to have proved the generalized version. GRH extends the original conjecture to related mathematical functions called Dirichlet L-functions. German mathematician Bernhard Riemann introduced his original hypothesis in 1859. It proposes that every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function lies on a specific vertical line. That line has a real component of exactly one-half. The conjecture connects prime number distribution with the behavior of this complex mathematical function. Its implications reach across number theory, including results that researchers have established conditionally. The Clay Mathematics Institute recognizes the Riemann hypothesis as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems. Each carries a $1 million award. articles.title: Behind the World's Softest Fiber: How Peru Is Using Genomics to Dominate Luxury Textiles
articles.desc: UNALM, Inca Tops and MGI Tech are sequencing 1,200 alpaca genomes in Puno to identify superior breeders earlier and strengthen Peru's position in the global fiber market.
articles.content: Behind the World's Softest Fiber: How Peru Is Using Genomics to Dominate Luxury Textiles UNALM, Inca Tops, and MGI Tech are jointly sequencing 1,200 alpaca samples at the Pacomarca research station in Puno, with the goal of identifying top breeders from birth rather than through post-shearing laboratory analysis. Each animal generates approximately 2.6 gigabytes of genomic data, processed through MGI's DNBSEQ T7RS platform; the first genetically selected breeders are expected by mid-2027, with superior offspring reaching highland producers by 2028. Peru holds approximately 87% of the world's alpaca population, with a national herd of around 4.7 million animals, and exported $238 million in alpaca products in 2025, up 6.5% from 2024, according to the Alpaca Industry Association, citing PromPerú's annual report. A three-way scientific alliance is sequencing the genomes of 1,200 Peruvian alpacas — hunting for the precise genetic markers that produce the world's softest fiber and could cement Peru's control over a sector that With luxury fashion houses in Europe, the United States, and Asia intensifying their competition for premium natural fibers, the ability to breed genetically superior alpacas from birth — rather than identify them years later after shearing — could permanently reshape who leads the The challenge isn't simply making fiber finer — it's eliminating the specific strands that make it scratch. Alpaca fleece can carry a share of strongly medullated fibers, whose hollow, rigid internal structure creates the skin irritation luxury buyers penalize most heavily. Detecting which animals naturally produce fewer of those problematic strands has historically required laboratory tests performed after shearing — a workflow that is slow, expensive, and largely out of reach for the thousands of smallholder producers farming across Peru's high Andes. The genomic project flips that model entirely: instead of assessing animals after the fact, researchers aim to identify superior breeders through DNA analysis from the moment of birth. From Puno's Highlands to a Genomic Pipeline , Inca Tops' dedicated facility in Puno — the region that holds the country's largest concentration of the national alpaca herd. The station houses an average of 2,500 alpacas annually, maintains working relationships with more than 1,000 local families, and purchases raw fiber from approximately 8,000 smallholder producers. Once collected, samples move through MGI's automated MGISP-960RS processing system before being read by the DNBSEQ T7RS sequencer. The MegaBOLT bioinformatics accelerator then links each animal's genetic blueprint to its physical fineness measurements, producing an individual genetic value score. from birth," said Gustavo Gutiérrez, a researcher collaborating with the UNALM team from the United States, arguing that earlier identification will sharpen breeder selection and generate direct economic benefits for highland communities. The Commercial Stakes Behind Every Base Pair Peru's structural dominance in the global fiber supply chain is difficult to overstate. The country holds 87% of the world's alpaca population, with a national herd of approximately 4.7 million animals — a concentration built over millennia of Andean husbandry and impossible to replicate elsewhere at scale. reached $238 million in 2025, growing 6.5% from the prior year, as buyers in China, the United States, Italy, and other key markets expanded their demand for , yarn, and processed fiber. Genetic-selection programs reinforce that trajectory by improving fiber uniformity, reducing specification risk, and enabling processors to offer more dependable supply commitments to international buyers.
